CveFindings.Name: Improper Handling of Exceptional Conditions in Newtonsoft.Json
CveFindings.Description:
[CVE-2024-21907](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5crp-9r3c-p9vr): Newtonsoft.Json versions before 13.0.1 can cause denial of service through deeply nested or crafted JSON.

Severity: HIGH

Affected dependency: Newtonsoft.Json 12.0.1 (declared at src/eShopLegacyWebForms/packages.config:31).

Recommended fix: Upgrade to Newtonsoft.Json 13.0.1 or later, or enforce a suitable MaxDepth setting when deserializing untrusted data.

CweFindings.Name: Incorrect Conversion between Numeric Types
CweFindings.Description: When converting from one data type to another, such as long to integer, data can be omitted or translated in a way that produces unexpected values. If the resulting values are used in a sensitive context, then dangerous behaviors may occur.
CweFindings.Explanation: CatalogItemHiLoGenerator.GetNextSequenceValue and CatalogDBInitializer.GetSequenceIdFromSelectedDBSequence both cast database Int64 sequence values to Int32 without range checks. Values above Int32.MaxValue can wrap and produce incorrect identifiers.

CweFindings.Name: Use of Singleton Pattern Without Synchronization in a Multithreaded Context
CweFindings.Description: The product uses the singleton pattern when creating a resource within a multithreaded environment.
CweFindings.Explanation: When UseMockData is enabled, ApplicationModule registers CatalogServiceMock as an Autofac singleton (ApplicationModule.cs:18-22). Its catalogItems list is shared across requests; CreateCatalogItem, UpdateCatalogItem, RemoveCatalogItem and reads access or mutate it without synchronization (CatalogServiceMock.cs:12, 16, 19-21, 35, 48-66). Concurrent requests can race while enumerating or modifying the list.

CweFindings.Description: The product does not properly synchronize shared data, such as static variables across threads, which can lead to undefined behavior and unpredictable data changes.

CweFindings.Explanation: When UseMockData is enabled, ApplicationModule registers CatalogServiceMock as an Autofac singleton (ApplicationModule.cs:18-22). Its catalogItems list is shared across requests; CreateCatalogItem, UpdateCatalogItem, RemoveCatalogItem and reads access or mutate it without synchronization (CatalogServiceMock.cs:12, 16, 19-21, 35, 48-66). Concurrent requests can race while enumerating or modifying the list.
